I have 340 mu — that is a lot of land for one household, so I rent most of it and use machine services for plowing and harvest. Three years in, I mostly copy what the older growers around Quzhou do, and I change little things when I see something work on a neighbor's field. My main system is wheat-maize double cropping, which is what everyone does here. I keep a small piece in soybean to rest the soil a bit, and I try peanut for oil because the price has been decent and my uncle grows it.

For **winter wheat** on about 300 mu — I buy improved seed (Jimai or Shixin kind, whatever the dealer has), sow in early October after maize harvest. I put down compound fertilizer 50 kg/mu (15-15-15) as base, then top dress urea 20 kg/mu at jointing. That gives roughly 15 kg N, 7.5 kg P, 7.5 kg K per mu. I water at planting, then green-up, jointing, and filling — four times with the well. Spray herbicide once in spring, plus one fungicide/insecticide mix at heading. I expect about 500 kg/mu in a normal year.

For **summer maize** on 270 mu after the wheat — I use hybrid seed (Zhengdan or Xianyu type), no-till direct seed into the wheat stubble right after harvest. Base fertilizer 40 kg compound at sowing, then 25 kg urea at big-trumpet stage. One irrigation at tasseling if rain is short. Two sprays — one for armyworm/borer, one for leaf disease. Expect 550 kg/mu.

For **soybean** on 30 mu — I do not put much nitrogen, the plant makes its own. Just 25 kg compound at sowing. One irrigation, one spray for aphid. Expect 170 kg/mu.

For **peanut** (oilseed) on 40 mu — needs more potassium and calcium. I put 40 kg compound plus some gypsum. Two or three sprays because leaf spot is a problem here. Expect 280 kg/mu.

I would rather spend a bit extra on fertilizer than lose yield — a bad wheat harvest across 300 mu would ruin the year. But on this scale I cannot afford to waste either, so I stick close to what my neighbors do.
